Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Avery Hayes
Member ID: W671125198
Reference Number: POC-1F29AC6C03-84154
Date of Notice: 2026-08-09
Service: Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-05

To the Wellpoint Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-09 (Reference Number POC-1F29AC6C03-84154). The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree and ask that the plan reconsider this determination in light of the clinical documentation summarized below.

Medical policy applied

The denial notice does not name a specific medical policy document or policy number. Based on my own research, Wellpoint delegates prior-authorization and medical-necessity review for CPT 27702 to Carelon Medical Benefits Management, Inc., under the guideline titled "Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Small Joint Surgery" (Ankle Arthritis section; Doc ID MSK06-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025, last review date 04/21/2025), available at https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/small-joint-surgery-2025-11-15/. I was not able to confirm from a Georgia-specific Wellpoint publication that this exact guideline version was the one applied to my case, and I ask that Wellpoint identify, in writing, the specific policy document and version actually used to review my request, including its effective date, so that I and my surgeon can respond to it directly. Where I quote below, the quoted language is text I was able to locate in the publicly posted Carelon guideline; where I have not been able to locate and verify exact plan language, I say so and argue in my own words.

Response to the stated denial reason

1. Documentation requirements for conservative management. The guideline I located states that supporting documentation "must include the following components: Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented." My clinical record satisfies each of these elements:

  - Symptom duration and severity: 18 months of progressive ankle pain, unrelieved by rest, documented by Dr. Duval.
  - Functional limitations: Ambulation limited to two blocks with an antalgic gait; positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain.
  - Type and duration of therapeutic measures provided:
    - Supervised physical therapy targeting ankle strengthening and balance — 8 weeks, 24 completed visits, 2026-05-08 through 2026-07-03 (documented in the physical therapy discharge note).
    - NSAID therapy for 8 months, with inadequate relief.
    - Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08, producing only 3 weeks of partial relief.

2. Duration of conservative management. The guideline provision I located states that total ankle arthroplasty is medically necessary when, among other things, "Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)." My conservative treatment course — 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy plus 8 months of NSAID use plus a corticosteroid injection — extended well beyond 3 months, with documented inadequate and only transient relief. This directly satisfies the durational element of the criterion as I have located it.

3. Radiographic severity. The guideline provision I located requires "Radiographic confirmation of Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4 arthritis of the tibiotalar joint OR avascular necrosis of the talus." Weight-bearing ankle radiographs dated 2026-07-13 document tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts — findings consistent with severe (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3–4) tibiotalar arthritis. [Formal Kellgren-Lawrence grade to be confirmed in writing by the interpreting radiologist or Dr. Duval, as the clinical summary provided to me does not state the numeric grade.] If the plan's review did not credit these radiographic findings as meeting this criterion, I ask that it explain specifically why.

4. Vascular status. The guideline provision I located also references "Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses)." [Vascular examination findings, including pedal pulse status, are not included in the clinical summary provided to me; this documentation will be supplied by Dr. Duval as a supplement to this appeal.]

5. Absence of contraindications. My record reflects no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoking status. I am not able to quote the plan's specific contraindication language because I have not located and verified that text; I raise these facts only to show, in my own words, that common contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty do not appear to be present in my case, and I ask the plan to identify any contraindication it believes applies.

Conclusion

Taken together, the records show 18 months of progressive symptoms, a supervised and adequately documented trial of physical therapy, prolonged NSAID use, and a corticosteroid injection — all with inadequate or only temporary relief — together with radiographic evidence of severe tibiotalar joint destruction. I believe this documentation addresses the stated reason for denial and satisfies the medical-necessity elements set out above. I ask that Wellpoint reverse its determination and approve the requested total ankle replacement (CPT 27702).

Enclosed with this appeal are the following records: physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-08 to 2026-07-03), medication history documenting NSAID use and corticosteroid injection, weight-bearing ankle radiograph report dated 2026-07-13, and clinical/exam notes from Dr. Duval. [Additional vascular exam documentation and formal Kellgren-Lawrence grading to be submitted by Dr. Duval, as noted above.]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide written notice of the outcome within the timeframe required by applicable law and the plan's appeal procedures. If any portion of this appeal must be directed to a different address, fax number, or online portal than the one used above, please notify me immediately given the 2027-02-05 appeal deadline stated in the original notice.

Sincerely,

Avery Hayes
Member ID: W671125198
